name: file_organizer
spec: Create a command-line file system organizer in Python using only the standard library. The tool scans a target directory and organizes files into subdirectories based on configurable rules (by file type, date, size, or name pattern). It supports a dry-run mode to preview changes before applying them and keeps a log of all operations for undo support.
features: Accepts a target directory path as a command-line argument
Scans the directory and lists all files with their type, size, and modification date
Organizes files into subdirectories by file extension category (e.g. Images, Documents, Audio, Video, Code, Other)
Supports organizing by modification date into year/month subdirectories with a --by-date flag
Supports organizing by file size into Small/Medium/Large subdirectories with a --by-size flag
Supports a dry-run mode with --dry-run flag that shows what would happen without moving files
Displays a summary showing how many files would be moved to each subdirectory
Handles filename conflicts by appending a number suffix (e.g. file_1.txt, file_2.txt)
Logs all file operations to a JSON log file with source and destination paths
Supports an undo command that reads the log and reverses the last organization operation
Skips hidden files and directories by default
Handles permission errors gracefully with a warning message per file
Shows a progress indicator when processing large directories
